newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says Iraq-based rebel surrenders to troops.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Iraq-based rebel surrenders to troops.

text.p: Iran said on Friday a member of an Iraq-based armed opposition group surrendered to the authorities after killing a comrade.
The Iranian news agency IRNA quoted an unnamed security official as saying the Mujahideen Khalq member had killed the man "in a wrangle" after crossing together into Iran.

Tehran has said its troops killed several Mujahideen members in clashes in western Iran in the past few weeks. The Mujahideen have admitted that some of their forces were killed but said they had slain dozens of government troops.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its forces.

Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years. The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for hitting military, government and economic targets.
